citations.short: Procedures not  in writing, fully followed
citations.long: The responsibilities and procedures applicable to the quality control unit are not in writing.
Protective apparel is not worn as necessary to protect drug products from contamination.
Aseptic processing areas are deficient regarding the system for cleaning and disinfecting the room to produce aseptic conditions.
Written procedures for sanitation are not followed.
Written production and process control procedures are not followed in the execution of production and process control functions.
Written production and control procedures include batches formulated with the intent to provide less than 100 percent of the labeled or established amount of active ingredient.
Procedures designed to prevent microbiological contamination of drug products purporting to be sterile are not written.
There is a failure to thoroughly review any unexplained discrepancy whether or not the batch has been already distributed.
Procedures describing the handling of written and oral complaints related to drug products are deficiently written or followed.
Employees are not given training in the particular operations they perform as part of their function.
Equipment and utensils are not cleaned at appropriate intervals to prevent contamination that would alter the safety, identity, strength, quality or purity of the drug product.

citations.short: Written calibration / inspection records not  kept
citations.long: Records of the calibration checks and inspections of automatic, mechanical or electronic equipment, including computers or related systems are not maintained.

citations.short: Changes to Procedures Not Reviewed, Approved
citations.long: Changes to written procedures are not reviewed and approved by the quality control unit.
The written stability program for drug products does not include reliable, meaningful, and specific test methods.
Each batch of drug product purporting to be sterile and pyrogen-free is not laboratory tested to determine conformance to such requirements.
Investigations of an unexplained discrepancy did not extend to other batches of the same drug product and other drug products that may have been associated with the specific failure or discrepancy.
Written records are not made of investigations into unexplained discrepancies and the failure of a batch or any of its components to meet specifications.
